candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / De Incarnatione Verbi §17
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §17 (c. 350 AD)

'By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah' — Athanasius marks tois en phylakē pneumasin poreutheis ekēryxen (the spirits in prison having-gone he-preached-to-them) as the HARROWING-OF-HADES anchor: the Word's-soul (united-to-the-Word's-divinity even through the three-day-burial-pause) travels to release the OT-righteous (and to confront the OT-disobedient — the antediluvian-spirits) in the inter-mortem state. The Word does NOT release-himself from the body (the Word remains-united-to-flesh even in the tomb); rather, the unified-Christ-in-his-soul descends-to-Hades while-the-body-rests-in-the-tomb. The harrowing is the inaugural-moment of the Word's-Paschal-Cosmic-Victory. Tewahedo Holy-Saturday iconography (Anastasis-icon: Christ pulling Adam + Eve out of the tomb) preserves this 1 Peter 3:19-anchored harrowing-tradition.
